passages.text: Then Moses answered, “What if they do not believe me or listen to my voice? For they may say, ‘The LORD has not appeared to you.’ ”
passages.sermon:
Moses was a Hebrew man.
God spoke to Moses at the burning bush.
God told Moses to lead the Israelites out of Egypt.
Moses answered God.
Moses said, “They will not believe me.”
Moses said, “They will not listen to my voice.”
Moses said, “They may say, ‘The LORD has not appeared to you.’”
passages.original: וַיַּ֤עַן מֹשֶׁה֙ וַיֹּ֔אמֶר וְהֵן֙ לֹֽא־ יַאֲמִ֣ינוּ לִ֔י וְלֹ֥א יִשְׁמְע֖וּ בְּקֹלִ֑י כִּ֣י יֹֽאמְר֔וּ לֹֽא־ נִרְאָ֥ה אֵלֶ֖יךָ יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: And the LORD asked him, “What is that in your hand?” “A staff,” he replied.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Moses.
The LORD asked Moses a question.
The LORD said, “What is that in your hand?”
Moses answered the LORD.
Moses said, “A staff.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר אֵלָ֛יו יְהוָ֖ה מַזֶּה בְיָדֶ֑ךָ וַיֹּ֖אמֶר מַטֶּֽה׃

passages.text: “Throw it on the ground,” said the LORD. So Moses threw it on the ground, and it became a snake, and he ran from it.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Moses.
The LORD said, "Throw it on the ground."
Moses obeyed the LORD.
Moses threw his staff on the ground.
The staff became a snake.
Moses saw the snake.
Moses ran away from the snake.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ הַשְׁלִיכֵ֣הוּ אַ֔רְצָה וַיַּשְׁלִיכֵ֥הוּ אַ֖רְצָה וַיְהִ֣י לְנָחָ֑שׁ וַיָּ֥נָס מֹשֶׁ֖ה מִפָּנָֽיו׃

passages.text: “Stretch out your hand and grab it by the tail,” the LORD said to Moses, who reached out his hand and caught the snake, and it turned back into a staff in his hand.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Moses.
The LORD told Moses, "Stretch out your hand."
The LORD told Moses, "Grab the snake by its tail."
Moses stretched out his hand.
Moses grabbed the snake by its tail.
The snake turned back into a staff in Moses' hand.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־ מֹשֶׁ֔ה שְׁלַח֙ יָֽדְךָ֔ וֶאֱחֹ֖ז בִּזְנָב֑וֹ וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח יָדוֹ֙ וַיַּ֣חֲזֶק בּ֔וֹ וַיְהִ֥י לְמַטֶּ֖ה בְּכַפּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: “This is so that they may believe that the LORD, the God of their fathers—the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob—has appeared to you.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Moses.
The LORD is the God of Abraham.
The LORD is the God of Isaac.
The LORD is the God of Jacob.
The LORD is the God of their fathers.
The LORD appeared to Moses.
The LORD gave signs to Moses.
The LORD did this so the people would believe.
The people would believe that the LORD appeared to Moses.
passages.original: לְמַ֣עַן יַאֲמִ֔ינוּ כִּֽי־ נִרְאָ֥ה אֵלֶ֛יךָ יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י אֲבֹתָ֑ם אֱלֹהֵ֧י אַבְרָהָ֛ם אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִצְחָ֖ק וֵאלֹהֵ֥י יַעֲקֹֽב׃

passages.text: Furthermore, the LORD said to Moses, “Put your hand inside your cloak.” So he put his hand inside his cloak, and when he took it out, his hand was leprous, white as snow.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Moses.
The LORD is the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
The LORD told Moses to put his hand inside his cloak.
Moses put his hand inside his cloak.
Moses took his hand out of his cloak.
Moses saw his hand.
His hand was leprous.
His hand was white as snow.
passages.original: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ יְהוָ֨ה ל֜וֹ ע֗וֹד הָֽבֵא־ נָ֤א יָֽדְךָ֙ בְּחֵיקֶ֔ךָ וַיָּבֵ֥א יָד֖וֹ בְּחֵיק֑וֹ וַיּ֣וֹצִאָ֔הּ וְהִנֵּ֥ה יָד֖וֹ מְצֹרַ֥עַת כַּשָּֽׁלֶג׃

passages.text: “Put your hand back inside your cloak,” said the LORD. So Moses put his hand back inside his cloak, and when he took it out, it was restored, like the rest of his skin.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Moses.
The LORD told Moses to put his hand back inside his cloak.
Moses put his hand back inside his cloak.
Moses took his hand out from his cloak.
Moses saw that his hand was healed.
Moses' hand was like the rest of his skin.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הָשֵׁ֤ב יָֽדְךָ֙ אֶל־ חֵיקֶ֔ךָ וַיָּ֥שֶׁב יָד֖וֹ אֶל־ חֵיק֑וֹ וַיּֽוֹצִאָהּ֙ מֵֽחֵיק֔וֹ וְהִנֵּה־ שָׁ֖בָה כִּבְשָׂרֽוֹ׃

passages.text: And the LORD said, “If they refuse to believe you or heed the witness of the first sign, they may believe that of the second.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Moses.
The LORD gave Moses signs to show the people.
The LORD said, “Some people may not believe you at first.
They may not listen to the first sign.
But they may believe the second sign.”
passages.original: וְהָיָה֙ אִם־ לֹ֣א יַאֲמִ֣ינוּ לָ֔ךְ וְלֹ֣א יִשְׁמְע֔וּ לְקֹ֖ל הָאֹ֣ת הָרִאשׁ֑וֹן וְהֶֽאֱמִ֔ינוּ לְקֹ֖ל הָאֹ֥ת הָאַחֲרֽוֹן׃

passages.text: But if they do not believe even these two signs or listen to your voice, take some water from the Nile and pour it on the dry ground. Then the water you take from the Nile will become blood on the ground.”
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Moses.
God gave Moses signs to show the people.
God said, “If the people do not believe these two signs,
and if they do not listen to your voice,
take some water from the Nile River.
Pour the water on the dry ground.
The water you take from the Nile will become blood on the ground.”
passages.original: וְהָיָ֡ה אִם־ לֹ֣א יַאֲמִ֡ינוּ גַּם֩ לִשְׁנֵ֨י הָאֹת֜וֹת הָאֵ֗לֶּה וְלֹ֤א יִשְׁמְעוּן֙ לְקֹלֶ֔ךָ וְלָקַחְתָּ֙ מִמֵּימֵ֣י הַיְאֹ֔ר וְשָׁפַכְתָּ֖ הַיַּבָּשָׁ֑ה וְהָי֤וּ הַמַּ֙יִם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר תִּקַּ֣ח מִן־ הַיְאֹ֔ר וְהָי֥וּ לְדָ֖ם בַּיַּבָּֽשֶׁת׃

passages.text: “Please, Lord,” Moses replied, “I have never been eloquent, neither in the past nor since You have spoken to Your servant, for I am slow of speech and tongue.”
passages.sermon:
Moses was a man chosen by God to lead Israel.
Moses spoke to the Lord.
Moses said, “Please, Lord.”
Moses said, “I am not a man of words.”
Moses said, “I have never been eloquent.”
Moses said, “I was not eloquent yesterday.”
Moses said, “I was not eloquent the day before yesterday.”
Moses said, “I have not been eloquent since You spoke to Your servant.”
Moses said, “I am slow of speech.”
Moses said, “I am slow of tongue.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֣ה אֶל־ יְהוָה֮ בִּ֣י אֲדֹנָי֒ לֹא֩ אִ֨ישׁ דְּבָרִ֜ים אָנֹ֗כִי גַּ֤ם מִתְּמוֹל֙ גַּ֣ם מִשִּׁלְשֹׁ֔ם גַּ֛ם מֵאָ֥ז דַּבֶּרְךָ אֶל־ עַבְדֶּ֑ךָ כִּ֧י כְבַד־ פֶּ֛ה וּכְבַ֥ד לָשׁ֖וֹן אָנֹֽכִי׃

passages.text: And the LORD said to him, “Who gave man his mouth? Or who makes the mute or the deaf, the sighted or the blind? Is it not I, the LORD?
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Moses.
The LORD is God.
The LORD asked Moses a question.
The LORD said, “Who gives a person his mouth?”
The LORD said, “Who makes a person unable to speak?”
The LORD said, “Who makes a person deaf?”
The LORD said, “Who makes a person able to see?”
The LORD said, “Who makes a person blind?”
The LORD said, “I am the one who does these things.”
The LORD said, “I am the LORD.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֵלָ֗יו מִ֣י שָׂ֣ם פֶּה֮ לָֽאָדָם֒ א֚וֹ מִֽי־ יָשׂ֣וּם אִלֵּ֔ם א֣וֹ חֵרֵ֔שׁ א֥וֹ פִקֵּ֖חַ א֣וֹ עִוֵּ֑ר הֲלֹ֥א אָנֹכִ֖י יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: Now go! I will help you as you speak, and I will teach you what to say.”
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Moses.
God is the LORD.
God told Moses to go.
God said, “I will be with your mouth.”
God said, “I will help you speak.”
God said, “I will teach you what to say.”
passages.original: וְעַתָּ֖ה לֵ֑ךְ וְאָנֹכִי֙ אֶֽהְיֶ֣ה עִם־ פִּ֔יךָ וְהוֹרֵיתִ֖יךָ אֲשֶׁ֥ר תְּדַבֵּֽר׃

passages.text: But Moses replied, “Please, Lord, send someone else.”
passages.sermon:
Moses spoke to the Lord.
Moses said, "Please, Lord, send someone else."
Moses did not want to go.
Moses asked God to choose another person.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר בִּ֣י אֲדֹנָ֑י שְֽׁלַֽח־ נָ֖א בְּיַד־ תִּשְׁלָֽח׃

passages.text: Then the anger of the LORD burned against Moses, and He said, “Is not Aaron the Levite your brother? I know that he can speak well, and he is now on his way to meet you. When he sees you, he will be glad in his heart.
passages.sermon:
The LORD became angry with Moses.
The LORD spoke to Moses.
Aaron is your brother.
Aaron is a Levite.
I know Aaron can speak well.
Aaron is coming to meet you now.
When Aaron sees you, he will be glad in his heart.
passages.original: וַיִּֽחַר־ אַ֨ף יְהוָ֜ה בְּמֹשֶׁ֗ה וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ הֲלֹ֨א אַהֲרֹ֤ן אָחִ֙יךָ֙ הַלֵּוִ֔י יָדַ֕עְתִּי כִּֽי־ דַבֵּ֥ר יְדַבֵּ֖ר ה֑וּא וְגַ֤ם הִנֵּה־ הוּא֙ יֹצֵ֣א לִקְרָאתֶ֔ךָ וְרָאֲךָ֖ וְשָׂמַ֥ח בְּלִבּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: You are to speak to him and put the words in his mouth. I will help both of you to speak, and I will teach you what to do.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Moses.
God told Moses to speak to Aaron.
God told Moses to put the words in Aaron’s mouth.
God said, “I will help you speak.”
God said, “I will help Aaron speak.”
God said, “I will teach you both what to do.”
passages.original: וְדִבַּרְתָּ֣ אֵלָ֔יו וְשַׂמְתָּ֥ אֶת־ הַדְּבָרִ֖ים בְּפִ֑יו וְאָנֹכִ֗י אֶֽהְיֶ֤ה עִם־ פִּ֙יךָ֙ וְעִם־ פִּ֔יהוּ וְהוֹרֵיתִ֣י אֶתְכֶ֔ם אֵ֖ת אֲשֶׁ֥ר תַּעֲשֽׂוּן׃

passages.text: He will speak to the people for you. He will be your spokesman, and it will be as if you were God to him.
passages.sermon:
Aaron is your brother.
Aaron is a Levite.
Aaron will speak to the people for you.
Aaron will be your spokesman.
You will be like God to Aaron.
passages.original: וְדִבֶּר־ ה֥וּא לְךָ֖ אֶל־ הָעָ֑ם וְהָ֤יָה הוּא֙ יִֽהְיֶה־ לְּךָ֣ לְפֶ֔ה וְאַתָּ֖ה תִּֽהְיֶה־ לּ֥וֹ לֵֽאלֹהִֽים׃

passages.text: But take this staff in your hand so you can perform signs with it.”
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Moses.
God told Moses to take the staff.
God said, “Take this staff in your hand.”
God said, “You will use this staff.”
God said, “You will perform signs with this staff.”
passages.original: וְאֶת־ הַמַּטֶּ֥ה הַזֶּ֖ה תִּקַּ֣ח בְּיָדֶ֑ךָ אֲשֶׁ֥ר תַּעֲשֶׂה־ בּ֖וֹ אֶת־ הָאֹתֹֽת׃פ

passages.text: Then Moses went back to his father-in-law Jethro and said to him, “Please let me return to my brothers in Egypt to see if they are still alive.” “Go in peace,” Jethro replied.
passages.sermon:
Moses was a prophet of God.
Jethro was Moses’ father-in-law.
Moses went to Jethro.
Moses spoke to Jethro.
Moses said, “Please let me return to my brothers in Egypt.
I want to see if they are still alive.”
Jethro answered Moses.
Jethro said, “Go in peace.”
passages.original: וַיֵּ֨לֶךְ מֹשֶׁ֜ה וַיָּ֣שָׁב׀ אֶל־ יֶ֣תֶר חֹֽתְנ֗וֹ וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לוֹ֙ אֵ֣לֲכָה נָּ֗א וְאָשׁ֙וּבָה֙ אֶל־ אַחַ֣י אֲשֶׁר־ בְּמִצְרַ֔יִם וְאֶרְאֶ֖ה הַעוֹדָ֣ם חַיִּ֑ים וַיֹּ֧אמֶר יִתְר֛וֹ לְמֹשֶׁ֖ה לֵ֥ךְ לְשָׁלֽוֹם׃

passages.text: Now the LORD had said to Moses in Midian, “Go back to Egypt, for all the men who sought to kill you are dead.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Moses in Midian.
The LORD told Moses to return to Egypt.
The LORD said all the men who wanted to kill Moses are dead.
Moses no longer needed to fear those men in Egypt.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֤ה אֶל־ מֹשֶׁה֙ בְּמִדְיָ֔ן לֵ֖ךְ שֻׁ֣ב מִצְרָ֑יִם כִּי־ מֵ֙תוּ֙ כָּל־ הָ֣אֲנָשִׁ֔ים הַֽמְבַקְשִׁ֖ים אֶת־ נַפְשֶֽׁךָ׃

passages.text: So Moses took his wife and sons, put them on a donkey, and headed back to Egypt. And he took the staff of God in his hand.
passages.sermon:
Moses was a prophet and leader of the Israelites.
Moses took his wife.
Moses took his sons.
Moses put his wife and sons on a donkey.
Moses started to return to Egypt.
Moses took the staff of God in his hand.
passages.original: וַיִּקַּ֨ח מֹשֶׁ֜ה אֶת־ אִשְׁתּ֣וֹ וְאֶת־ בָּנָ֗יו וַיַּרְכִּבֵם֙ עַֽל־ הַחֲמֹ֔ר וַיָּ֖שָׁב אַ֣רְצָה מִצְרָ֑יִם וַיִּקַּ֥ח מֹשֶׁ֛ה אֶת־ מַטֵּ֥ה הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים בְּיָדֽוֹ׃

passages.text: The LORD instructed Moses, “When you go back to Egypt, see that you perform before Pharaoh all the wonders that I have put within your power. But I will harden his heart so that he will not let the people go.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Moses.
Moses was returning to Egypt.
The LORD gave Moses instructions.
The LORD told Moses to perform wonders before Pharaoh.
The LORD had given Moses power to do these wonders.
The LORD said He would harden Pharaoh’s heart.
Pharaoh would not let the people go.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָה֮ אֶל־ מֹשֶׁה֒ בְּלֶכְתְּךָ֙ לָשׁ֣וּב מִצְרַ֔יְמָה רְאֵ֗ה כָּל־ הַמֹּֽפְתִים֙ אֲשֶׁר־ שַׂ֣מְתִּי בְיָדֶ֔ךָ וַעֲשִׂיתָ֖ם לִפְנֵ֣י פַרְעֹ֑ה וַאֲנִי֙ אֲחַזֵּ֣ק אֶת־ לִבּ֔וֹ וְלֹ֥א יְשַׁלַּ֖ח אֶת־ הָעָֽם׃

passages.text: Then tell Pharaoh that this is what the LORD says: ‘Israel is My firstborn son, and I told you to let My son go so that he may worship Me. But since you have refused to let him go, behold, I will kill your firstborn son!’ ”
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Moses.
The LORD gave Moses a message for Pharaoh.
The LORD said, “Israel is My firstborn son.
I told you, Pharaoh, to let My son go.
I told you to let Israel go so that he may worship Me.
You refused to let him go.
Because you refused, I will kill your firstborn son.”
passages.original: וְאָמַרְתָּ֖ אֶל־ פַּרְעֹ֑ה כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה בְּנִ֥י בְכֹרִ֖י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ וָאֹמַ֣ר אֵלֶ֗יךָ שַׁלַּ֤ח אֶת־ בְּנִי֙ וְיַֽעַבְדֵ֔נִי וַתְּמָאֵ֖ן לְשַׁלְּח֑וֹ הִנֵּה֙ אָנֹכִ֣י הֹרֵ֔ג אֶת־ בִּנְךָ֖ בְּכֹרֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: Now at a lodging place along the way, the LORD met Moses and was about to kill him.
passages.sermon:
Moses traveled on the road.
He stopped at a lodging place.
The LORD met Moses there.
The LORD intended to kill Moses.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֥י בַדֶּ֖רֶךְ בַּמָּל֑וֹן וַיִּפְגְּשֵׁ֣הוּ יְהוָ֔ה וַיְבַקֵּ֖שׁ הֲמִיתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: But Zipporah took a flint knife, cut off her son’s foreskin, and touched it to Moses’ feet. “Surely you are a bridegroom of blood to me,” she said.
passages.sermon:
Zipporah was Moses’ wife.
She took a flint knife.
She cut off her son’s foreskin.
She touched the foreskin to Moses’ feet.
She said, “You are a bridegroom of blood to me.”
passages.original: וַתִּקַּ֨ח צִפֹּרָ֜ה צֹ֗ר וַתִּכְרֹת֙ אֶת־ עָרְלַ֣ת בְּנָ֔הּ וַתַּגַּ֖ע לְרַגְלָ֑יו וַתֹּ֕אמֶר כִּ֧י חֲתַן־ דָּמִ֛ים אַתָּ֖ה לִֽי׃

passages.text: So the LORD let him alone. (When she said, “bridegroom of blood,” she was referring to the circumcision.)
passages.sermon: The LORD stopped threatening Moses.\r\nZipporah had called Moses “bridegroom of blood.”\r\nShe meant this because of the circumcision.
passages.original: וַיִּ֖רֶף מִמֶּ֑נּוּ אָ֚ז אָֽמְרָ֔ה חֲתַ֥ן דָּמִ֖ים לַמּוּלֹֽת׃פ

passages.text: Meanwhile, the LORD had said to Aaron, “Go and meet Moses in the wilderness.” So he went and met Moses at the mountain of God and kissed him.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Aaron.
The LORD told Aaron to go and meet Moses in the wilderness.
Aaron obeyed the LORD.
Aaron went to find Moses.
Aaron met Moses at the mountain of God.
Aaron kissed Moses.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶֽל־ אַהֲרֹ֔ן לֵ֛ךְ לִקְרַ֥את מֹשֶׁ֖ה הַמִּדְבָּ֑רָה וַיֵּ֗לֶךְ וַֽיִּפְגְּשֵׁ֛הוּ בְּהַ֥ר הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים וַיִּשַּׁק־ לֽוֹ׃

passages.text: And Moses told Aaron everything the LORD had sent him to say, and all the signs He had commanded him to perform.
passages.sermon:
Moses was a prophet chosen by God.
Aaron was Moses’ brother.
The LORD had sent Moses with a message.
The LORD had also given Moses signs to perform.
Moses told Aaron everything the LORD had sent him to say.
Moses also told Aaron about all the signs the LORD had commanded him to perform.
passages.original: וַיַּגֵּ֤ד מֹשֶׁה֙ לְאַֽהֲרֹ֔ן אֵ֛ת כָּל־ דִּבְרֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר שְׁלָח֑וֹ וְאֵ֥ת כָּל־ הָאֹתֹ֖ת אֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוָּֽהוּ׃

passages.text: Then Moses and Aaron went and assembled all the elders of the Israelites, and Aaron relayed everything the LORD had said to Moses. And Moses performed the signs before the people, and they believed. And when they heard that the LORD had attended to the Israelites and had seen their affliction, they bowed down and worshiped.
passages.sermon:
Moses and Aaron were leaders chosen by God.
They went to the elders of the Israelites.
They gathered all the elders together.
Aaron spoke to the elders.
Aaron told them everything the LORD had said to Moses.
Moses showed the signs God had commanded.
He did these signs in front of the people.
The people saw the signs.
The people believed.
The people heard that the LORD cared for the Israelites.
They heard that the LORD saw their suffering.
The people bowed down.
They worshiped God.
passages.original: וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ מֹשֶׁ֖ה וְאַהֲרֹ֑ן וַיַּ֣אַסְפ֔וּ אֶת־ כָּל־ זִקְנֵ֖י בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר אַהֲרֹ֔ן אֵ֚ת כָּל־ הַדְּבָרִ֔ים אֲשֶׁר־ דִּבֶּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־ מֹשֶׁ֑ה וַיַּ֥עַשׂ הָאֹתֹ֖ת לְעֵינֵ֥י הָעָֽם׃ וַֽיַּאֲמֵ֖ן הָעָ֑ם וַֽיִּשְׁמְע֡וּ כִּֽי־ פָקַ֨ד יְהוָ֜ה אֶת־ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל וְכִ֤י רָאָה֙ אֶת־ עָנְיָ֔ם וַֽיִּקְּד֖וּ וַיִּֽשְׁתַּחֲוּֽוּ׃
